correctness.rationale: For disjoint pairs within each agent, deleting any one good eliminates at most one completed complementary pair, so EF1 is equivalent to cross-signature c<=a+1 and d<=b+1. Two coloured matchings form a multigraph of maximum degree two; alternating paths and cycles, including shared parallel pairs, can be processed edge-by-edge by a transfer DP retaining four utility/cross-valuation counters and two boundary labels. Identical states have identical possible future increments; this establishes full signature coverage and O(g^5) transitions/O(g^4) live states. Pareto filtering over all attainable own-utility pairs, rather than maximal welfare alone, correctly decides EF1+PO. A 2ell alternating cycle has only two perfect matching monopolies at welfare ell; a balanced contiguous split yields EF1 welfare ell−1, PO for ell>=3, while ell=2 is impossible, ell=1 succeeds. Independent full enumeration confirmed cycles ell=1..5 and the eight-good shared-pair-plus-six-cycle obstruction with PO frontier {(4,0),(3,1),(1,3),(0,4)}.
residual_risks: Requires exactly two agents and each agent’s own pair set a matching, unit weight additive over completed pairs.

originality.rationale: Qualified originality. Pyne–Viswanathan–Yang–Zick 2026 Proposition 2.1 explicitly supplies the four-good alternating-cycle EF1+PO impossibility; that is recognized as known, not new. The fully rendered same-model source develops arbitrary binary SPOC hardness and welfare approximations/EFX, but its statements and inspected sections do not give the exact two-agent free-matroid disjoint-pair signature DP, all-cycle phase boundary or eight-good disconnected obstruction. A strictly increasing valuation EF1+PO result requires positive singleton marginal values and cannot apply to pair complements. A differently phrased bounded-treewidth fair-allocation DP may be a priority antecedent.
residual_risks: A generic degree-two/treewidth signature-DP theorem for specialized EF1+PO could already imply the construction.
The ℓ=2 counterexample is known and is not treated as the novel finding.

value.rationale: Pair complements create a substantive fairness/efficiency incompatibility even with only two agents, as the primary 2026 paper demonstrates. The disjoint-pair/free-matroid subclass is a natural boundary of this hardness. An exact O(g^5) decision and witness construction for all inputs, a sharp connected-cycle phase law, and an unexpected disconnected obstruction clarify which structural conditions do and do not restore fair efficient allocations; these are nontrivial algorithmic and structural facts.
residual_risks: Generality stops at two agents with additive disjoint-pair values; no NP-hard general SPOC problem is solved.

limitations: Only two agents, unit additive complementary pairs disjoint within each agent, complete allocation.
The four-good ℓ=2 obstruction is explicitly known from Pyne et al.; only new wider classification and algorithm assessed.
